newsitem.title: USA: Ciena files 10 mln share secondary offer.
newsitem.headline: Ciena files 10 mln share secondary offer.

text.p: Ciena Corp said Tuesday it had filed for a proposed secondary offering of about one million shares of common stock by the company and nine million shares by certain selling stockholders.
The offering is to be made through underwriters led by Goldman, Sachs & Co, Alex. Brown & Sons Inc and Wessels, Arnold & Henderson.

Separately, Ciena said it has signed a trial evaluation agreement with AT&T Corp through which Ciena will supply AT&T with its dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM). Ciena said the system passed AT&T's preliminary evaluation.
The Ciena system would allow AT&T to expand the capacity of high volume fiber optic lines in the backbone of the AT&T long distance network, a Ciena spokesman said.
AT&T has been evaluating DWDM system products, with enhancements to enable the use of multiple vendors in an open architecture, for deployment in its network.
"We've been pleased by CIENA's products and are very encouraged by the capacity and reliability the MultiWave system can offer us," said George Gawrys, Manager of Transport Planning for AT&T.
"AT&T is moving quickly to be sure our overall network capacity keeps pace with our customers' needs, and CIENA's MultiWave(TM) can be important in helping us achieve that goal," he said.
The trial evaluation deal is being undertaken with a view toward possible implementation starting in 1998, Ciena said.
Ciena fell 1-1/4 in early trading Tuesday to 45-7/8 after closing just off its all-time high on Monday.

The company debuted as a public company in February. Its backers boasted that its $3.7 billion market capitalization at the end of the first day of trading made it the largest valuation of a venture-capital backed start-up in history.
